On Q1/Q2 and the worked-example piece on our side (anchoring the twelve `evidence_sha256` values, the proof-blob shape, the ordering semantics): we're not picking that up right now — OT/building automation is a new domain for us without a concrete reason to prioritize it today. changes.author: giskard09
changes.title: Potential settlement-ordering issue: paid responses/tools can be released when credit settlement fails
changes.text:
igor-vii's NV-F1 in #503 is a concrete instance of what's described above: no idempotency key, no settlement-query API, and the only reconciliation artifact (the receipt header) is attached to exactly the response that got lost — so a retry re-settles instead of resolving to the same outcome.

The construction proposed above would address that directly: binding the idempotency key to `action_ref` means a retry resolves to the same record instead of minting a new billable attempt, and anchoring that record gives a third party something to check reconciliation against without trusting either sid

changes.author: giskard09
changes.title: Well-known entry at /.well-known/x402: shape and alignment with x402
changes.text:
One data point that hasn't come up yet in this thread: whatever shape the `/.well-known/x402` entry ends up taking (pointer vs. document), if it's ever hashed, anchored or used to detect drift between hosts, canonical encoding needs to be nailed down from day one — key ordering and whitespace alone can produce divergent hashes for byte-identical semantic content.

We hit this for a related manifest (`.well-known/agent.json` / `.well-known/mcp.json`) and serve both JCS-canonicalized (RFC 8785 — sorted keys, no whitespace, UTF-8) since July. Verified `raw_sha256 == canonical_sha256` in productio
